podcast.body: A solo album recorded under the alias "Late." Dave Grohl recorded four songs in December 1990, just a few months after joining Nirvana, and the remaining six songs were completed over two days in July 1991, about two months before Nirvana's *Nevermind* was released. It appeared on the "cheapo label" Simple Machines, run out of a house in Arlington, Virginia. The album, which credits "Dave G" on all instruments, didn't get much attention due to Dave's insistence; he didn't want to be seen as "crashing the party" with his own material as Nirvana was taking off. The label, Simple Machines, begged him to release it on CD, but it remained a cassette-only release. "If you look at the liner notes of Pocketwatch, you'll see that all performances on all instruments are credited to one Dave G."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This ten-song cassette-only album was released by Dave Grohl in the summer of 1991 under the name Late, before he joined Nirvana. Supply was very limited due to his increasing commitments with Nirvana, and he entrusted his friend Jenny Toomey, who ran the no-budget label Simple Machines, to make dubs until the master cassettes wore out. Grohl later refused requests to re-release it on vinyl or CD, preferring it to remain a cassette-only item. "He called the album Pocket Watch. Now supply was very limited, and Dave was getting busier with Nirvana, so he really didn't have much time to devote to his own stuff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
